results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 60 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs p01-p60, in spec order; the three intro callouts align to no spec paragraph.

The two units the outliner marked two_ideas (Introduction ¶2: volume plus the fiction disclaimer; In Transit ¶2: three notifications plus one record for status page and agent) each carry exactly the two parts the spec's own controlling idea for p02 and p34 joins; no other unit was marked.

Every unit serves a supporting claim: the owner table and p10 serve S1, the step table and the walk serve S2, p27/p50/p51 serve S3, p45-p46 serve S4, p47-p48 serve S5; intro and conclusion units carry the thesis.

Each table is introduced and read (p09-p10, p11-p12, p45-p46, p47-p48), each figure has a stated point, and each statistic and quotation (Baymard, Dutch Payments Association, Mollie, Stripe, Shopify, Gorgias, DeHoratius and Raman, PostNL 97%, IFRS 15, Odoo, 24% returns) is followed by what it shows for this order.

Every declared transition_in (paragraph and section level, introduction and conclusion) is expressed at its boundary: e.g. 'So what has to go right' (problem_solution), 'None was live for Eva's actual April order' (contrast), 'Because checkout only orchestrates' (cause_effect), 'The parcel's journey ends at the door. The order's does not.' (contrast), 'Those requirements describe the late-2027 design' (contrast).

Both flow readers describe the declared organising principle (setup, chronological walk, then grouped read-back) and mark no section's position unclear; their remaining lost-thread points other than those failed below are known terms or incidents on audience.already_knows (W-codes, Duiven, iPaaS, Three-Status Order, Black Friday Oversell, Sanne de Wit, scale stages, Giant's Boots) or a resolved re-read of the replay premise.
The introduction opens on Eva's concrete purchase and its two dangers, bridges via 293,000 orders a year, states the thesis and gives a roadmap; no weak pattern.
The conclusion synthesizes rather than restates, separates established from context-dependent points, and ends with a course of action and a hand-off; no weak pattern.

p55 sets late-2027 against January 2027 on the same systems and answers the so-what: 'A merchant that checks these four things on one ordinary order finds its next incidents before its customers do, and before it buys another system.'
p55: 'The two dangers named at the start, a wrong stock answer and a late warehouse instruction, are both joins: the stock copy and the fulfillment order.'

The intro reader predicted the section order exactly as the roadmap promises (owners, step table, search to books, handoff requirements, January 2027 replay, five failures), the thesis, the 293,000-order stakes and the evidence (replayed order, vendor documentation, official rules).

The reader located the duplicate parcels at the order handoff (no idempotency key on the order number, count of received against created) and the stuck iDEAL orders at the PSP webhook (outcome from webhook not browser, status fetched, Mollie's retries, daily sweep within the expiry window, mark paid once, webhooks never replace reconciliation), as expected.

The reader assigned PIM, platform price list, WMS, availability service, OMS (separate money, goods, returns), PSP (reference on order) and ERP (gap-free numbering) as expected, stated copies allowed but no second writer, and named invoice posting and payouts as batch and availability and the fulfillment order as events, with the reasons.

The reader answered: promised Wednesday, picked Wednesday and delivered Thursday because the static sentence ignores the 21:00 last wave; the promise should come from a delivery-promise service using the wave and the 22:30 collection; 'in stock' is a copy up to two hours old (Black Friday Oversell) and should be available-to-promise from the availability service fed by WMS stock events, seconds old, with a per-channel buffer.
